title: ExecutionRecord
description: Complete record of one execution (possibly several attempts).

extracted.description: Extracted variable names (values are run-local and not persisted here).

Id.description: Stable object identifier. UUIDv7 so ids sort roughly by creation time.

PreparedSummary.description:
Summary of the prepared request as it was actually sent (redacted).

`method`, `url`, `headers`, the body fields, `content_type` and
`auth_label` describe the original request as prepared; each attempt
records what it sent to its own target. `tls_profile`, `proxy` and
`tls_verification_enabled` describe the connection that produced the
final response (the last redirect hop when redirects were followed).

tls_profile.description:
TLS profile of the connection that produced the final response (the last redirect
hop when redirects were followed).

proxy.description:
Proxy route of the connection that produced the final response (the last redirect
hop when redirects were followed).

tls_verification_enabled.description:
Whether TLS verification was on for the connection that produced the
final response (the last redirect hop when redirects were followed).
`true` when that connection was plain HTTP: verification was not
turned off, there was no TLS to verify.

inferred.description: Headers Anvil added or inferred, and why.

omitted_secrets.description: Secrets omitted from this summary (labels only).

workload_api.description: SPIFFE Workload API calls and the SVIDs used (public data only).

Protocol.description:
Wire protocol family of a saved request. SOAP and GraphQL are HTTP body
kinds, not separate transports.

EffectiveSettings.description:
Fully-resolved settings used for one execution, with the layer each value
came from (for the Effective Request inspector).

early_data.description: 0-RTT early data policy (records written before it existed load as off).

HttpVersionPolicy.description: Protocol negotiation policy for HTTP-family requests.

oneOf.description: ALPN negotiation over TLS (h2, then http/1.1); HTTP/1.1 for cleartext.
HTTP/2 over TLS (ALPN `h2` only — fails rather than silently using HTTP/1.1).
Cleartext HTTP/2 with prior knowledge.
Forced HTTP/3 over QUIC. Never silently sends over TCP.
Try HTTP/3 first, then fall back to TCP; every attempt is recorded.

Timeouts.description:
Separate timeout classes. `None` means "no deadline for this phase" (the
total deadline still applies). Values are milliseconds.

request_write_ms.description: Deadline for handing the complete request (headers + body) to the connection.

response_headers_ms.description: Deadline from request sent to response headers.

body_idle_ms.description: Maximum idle gap between response body chunks.

forward_credentials_cross_origin.description:
Forward the request's credentials to a different origin: auth, a manual
`Cookie` header, credential or sensitive headers, headers holding a secret,
and a 307/308 body holding a secret. Off by default. The TLS client
identity is never forwarded: only a TLS profile bound to the new origin
presents one.

RetryPolicy.description:
Automatic retry policy. Off by default. Possibly-processed non-idempotent
operations are never retried automatically regardless of this setting.

only_safe.description:
Retained for compatibility. Retries are always limited to failures
proven `not_dispatched` or idempotent methods; a possibly processed
non-idempotent request is never replayed, whatever this says.

oneOf.description: Operating-system resolver (getaddrinfo).
Query the given DNS servers directly (`ip:port`), bypassing the OS resolver.

addresses.description: Addresses to connect to instead of resolving.

max_response_bytes.description:
Hard ceiling on response body bytes read from the wire; exceeded bodies
end with a local `response_too_large` outcome (never a peer fault).

capture_bytes.description:
Bytes retained for display/history; beyond this the body is still read
and counted but marked display-truncated.

EarlyDataPolicy.description:
TLS 1.3 / QUIC 0-RTT early data (RFC 8446 §2.3, RFC 9001 §4.6) with the
RFC 8470 semantics. Off by default: data sent before the handshake
completes can be replayed by anyone on the path, so only requests that are
safe to repeat may use it.

With `enabled`, a request whose method is eligible (GET, HEAD, OPTIONS, and
the idempotent methods listed in `extra_methods`) is sent as early data on
a new connection that resumes an earlier session of the same workspace, TLS
profile, client identity, server name and port. Any other method is sent
normally, after the handshake, and the record says why early data was not
used. A non-idempotent method in `extra_methods` is refused before traffic.

extra_methods.description:
Idempotent methods allowed in early data besides GET, HEAD and OPTIONS
(`PUT`, `DELETE`, `TRACE`). Only an explicit choice adds them.

WorkloadApiEvidence.description: Everything the Workload API contributed to one execution.

WorkloadApiCall.description: One Workload API call made for an execution.

endpoint.description: The endpoint dialed, as a URI (`unix:///run/spire/agent.sock`).

purpose.description: What the call was for (`TLS profile 'mesh client'`, `JWT-SVID auth`).

cached.description: Served from Anvil's in-memory cache (fetched by an earlier execution).

caller_uid.description:
The uid this process presents in the socket's peer credentials — what
a Workload API server attests. Recorded when no identity was issued.

oneOf.description: The profile's `endpoint` setting.
The `SPIFFE_ENDPOINT_SOCKET` environment variable.

WorkloadCallResult.description: What one Workload API call ended with.

oneOf.description: Anvil could not connect or speak HTTP/2 gRPC to the endpoint.
No answer within the deadline.

The endpoint answered with a non-OK gRPC status. `message` is the
endpoint's `grpc-message` (untrusted text, bounded).

An OK answer that carried no usable identity (no SVIDs, or none with
the requested SPIFFE ID).
The answer could not be decoded as the Workload API message.

X509SvidSummary.description: The X.509-SVID used as a TLS client identity (public data only).

chain_length.description: Certificates in the SVID chain (leaf first).

offered_spiffe_ids.description: SPIFFE IDs of every SVID the endpoint returned (the first is the default).

bundle_trusted.description: The SVID's trust-domain bundle was added to the profile's trust anchors.

federated_trust_domains.description:
Federated trust domains the endpoint also sent bundles for (recorded,
never trusted: one TLS profile holds one trust bundle).

refresh_after.description:
When Anvil will fetch a fresh SVID (half its lifetime, as SPIFFE
agents rotate).

JwtSvidSummary.description: The JWT-SVID Anvil presented (decoded claims only, never the token).

has_issuer.description: The token carries an `iss` claim (JWT-SVIDs define none).

sent_despite_failed_checks.description: The token was sent although a check failed (explicit profile choice).

oneOf.description: Three base64url segments with JSON header and claims.
`alg` present and asymmetric (never `none` or HMAC).
`sub` is a workload SPIFFE ID (and the configured one, when set).
Every requested audience is in `aud`.
`exp` present and in the future by this machine's clock.
Signature verified against the trust domain's JWT bundle.
Not evaluated (disabled, or an earlier check made it impossible).

early_data.description: 0-RTT early data evidence, when the early-data opt-in applied.

oneOf.description:
The previous attempt was eligible for early data and the server
answered `425 Too Early` (it did not process the request). Sent once
more after the handshake completed, never as early data (RFC 8470 §5.2).

FailureKind.description: Typed failure kinds. Rules match on these, never on message text.

oneOf.description:
The auth profile needs an interactive sign-in (OAuth authorization
code + PKCE) before a token exists; the request was not sent.

The SPIFFE Workload API endpoint could not be reached (no socket,
permission denied, nothing listening, not HTTP/2 gRPC, deadline).

The Workload API answered `PERMISSION_DENIED`, or an OK answer carried
no SVID for this caller: no identity was issued.
Any other Workload API failure (another gRPC status, a malformed answer).

A JWT-SVID failed Anvil's local checks (expiry, audience, subject,
algorithm, signature) and was not sent.

The mutual-TLS handshake with the HBONE endpoint failed. The precise
TLS cause is `connection.tunnel.failure` (and the tunnel's TLS
observation); the inner destination was never contacted.

The HBONE endpoint answered the HTTP/2 `CONNECT` with a non-2xx status
(kept, with the bounded body, in `connection.tunnel`).

HTTP/2 failure on the tunnel before a `CONNECT` status (no h2 ALPN,
preface/SETTINGS failure, stream reset, GOAWAY, deadline).

Peer sent a fatal alert after the client finished its handshake
(TLS 1.3 client-certificate rejection surfaces here).

SPIFFE verification: the X.509-SVID's SPIFFE ID differs from the
expected server SPIFFE ID (same trust domain).

SPIFFE verification: the server's SPIFFE ID belongs to a trust domain
the profile does not trust (or no configured bundle anchors it).

SPIFFE verification: the leaf is not a valid X.509-SVID (no URI SAN,
several URI SANs, or a malformed `spiffe://` ID).

The HTTP/3 MASQUE proxy's SETTINGS do not offer what the CONNECT-UDP
tunnel needs (extended CONNECT, or HTTP/3 datagrams when required),
or never arrived. No request was sent.

The MASQUE proxy answered the CONNECT-UDP request with a non-2xx
status; no tunnel was opened.

id.description: Engine-local connection id (stable within one app session).

prior_requests.description: Requests previously served on this connection (0 = fresh).

proxy_header.description: PROXY protocol header / datagram envelope Anvil sent, when enabled.

tunnel.description:
The tunnel the connection runs through: a mesh HBONE tunnel, or the
CONNECT-UDP (MASQUE) tunnel a DTLS session runs inside. Its outer
phases, TLS identities and `CONNECT` status are kept here, separate
from the inner connection's phases and TLS (`tls` above is the inner
TLS or DTLS with the destination).

sni.description:
The SNI actually sent in the ClientHello. `None` when the server name
is an IP address (TLS carries no IP SNI) or the handshake did not start.

server_name_overridden.description:
The SNI / verification name came from the TLS profile's
`server_name_override`, not from the URL host.

identity_check.description: The identity check the verifier applied (host name or SPIFFE).

peer_spiffe_id.description:
The peer leaf's SPIFFE ID (its single `spiffe://` URI SAN), recorded
for any TLS server that presents one, verified or not.

alpn_offered.description: ALPN protocols offered by the client.

peer_certificates.description: Peer chain as presented (leaf first), when received.

client_certificate_requested.description:
Whether the peer sent a CertificateRequest. `None` = not observed
(handshake did not get that far, or resumed session).

client_certificate_presented.description: The client certificate actually presented (public data only).

PeerIdentityCheck.description:
Which peer identity check the TLS verifier applied (or would have applied,
when verification is bypassed).

oneOf.description: RFC 6125 host-name (or IP address) verification against `name`.

SPIFFE X.509-SVID: the leaf's single URI SAN must equal `expected`
(which implies its trust domain). DNS names are not consulted.

SPIFFE X.509-SVID: the leaf's single URI SAN must be a SPIFFE ID in
`trust_domain`. DNS names are not consulted.

Verification disabled by an explicit, scoped bypass. Records what strict
verification would have concluded.
Handshake did not reach certificate verification.

ProxyHeaderObservation.description:
Exactly what PROXY protocol framing Anvil sent. Secrets never appear: the
authentication tag bytes are elided from `hex`, and any header bytes that
contain a redacted value are replaced as a whole.

length.description: Header length in bytes (for envelopes: of the first datagram's envelope).

hex.description:
The header bytes as hex (for envelopes: the first datagram's envelope
with the 32 tag bytes replaced by `‹tag›`).

tlvs.description: TLVs after the address block, summarized.

well_formed.description: The bytes satisfy the PROXY protocol specification as Anvil checks it.

listener_binding.description: `udp|dtls <bind address>:<port>` the tags were bound to.

datagrams.description: Datagrams sent with the envelope (handshake records included for DTLS).

oneOf.description: User-supplied bytes.
PROXY v2 `DGRAM` envelope on every datagram.
A relayed connection: the address block names the original client.

The balancer speaking for itself (health checks): no addresses are
sent and the receiver keeps the socket peer as the client.

AddressOrigin.description: Where a declared address came from.

oneOf.description: The real socket address of this connection.
Set explicitly in the request.

TunnelObservation.description: Evidence for the outer tunnel leg (Anvil ↔ tunnel endpoint).

endpoint.description: The tunnel endpoint (`host:port`) and the proxy profile label.

authority.description:
The inner destination: the HBONE `CONNECT` `:authority`, or the
CONNECT-UDP target (expanded into the request's `:path`).

phases.description:
Outer phases (DNS, TCP connect, mTLS handshake, HTTP/2 preface,
`CONNECT`; for CONNECT-UDP: DNS, the QUIC handshake, the proxy's
SETTINGS and the extended `CONNECT`), on the same clock as the
attempt's phases.

tls.description:
TLS with the endpoint: for HBONE the mutual TLS (client SVID presented,
the endpoint's verified server identity); for CONNECT-UDP the QUIC
handshake's TLS 1.3 with the proxy.

connect_headers.description: Non-pseudo headers sent on the `CONNECT` (markers, baggage, extras).

connect_status.description: Status the endpoint answered the `CONNECT` with, when one arrived.

refusal_body.description: Bounded UTF-8 (lossy) preview of a refusal body. Untrusted content.

failure.description:
The typed failure on the tunnel leg with its precise phase and kind
(e.g. `tls_spiffe_id_mismatch` at `tls_handshake`).

datagrams.description:
The datagram channel of a UDP tunnel (`CONNECT` with the `udp`
protocol marker); absent for a byte-stream tunnel.

oneOf.description: HTTP/2 `CONNECT` over mutual TLS (mesh HBONE).

HTTP/3 extended `CONNECT` with `:protocol = connect-udp` (RFC 9298
MASQUE): the QUIC connection to the proxy a DTLS session runs inside.
The tunnel's datagram accounting is in `ProtocolStatus::Udp::masque`.

PhaseTiming.description:
A measured phase. Offsets are microseconds from attempt start on a
monotonic clock. Concurrent phases may overlap; do not sum them blindly.

oneOf.description: Local validation / preparation (variables, files, profiles, signing).
Waiting for a pooled connection or a concurrency slot.
TCP connect (to the destination, or to the configured proxy).
Proxy tunnel establishment (HTTP CONNECT / SOCKS handshake).

PROXY protocol header written at the head of the connection (after
connect, before TLS).
Protocol handshake above TLS (HTTP/2 preface, WebSocket upgrade, ...).
Long-lived session (WebSocket / SSE / TCP / UDP / gRPC stream).
Satisfied by a reused connection; no new measurement exists.
Not part of this attempt (IP literal, cleartext, no body, ...).
Started but outcome unknown (e.g. the attempt was abandoned).

TransportFailure.description:
A typed transport failure with library detail for display. `message` is
sanitized display text only; diagnostic rules must use the typed fields.

tls_alert.description: TLS alert description (e.g. `certificate_required`) when one was received.

h2_error_code.description: HTTP/2 error code (RST_STREAM / GOAWAY) when applicable.

quic_error_code.description: QUIC transport/application error code when applicable.

status.description: HTTP status of a rejected proxy CONNECT / WebSocket handshake.

field.description: Field path for local validation failures (e.g. `headers[2].value`).

deadline_ms.description: The configured deadline that elapsed, for timeouts.

HboneDatagramChannel.description:
A UDP datagram channel carried by an HBONE `CONNECT` stream (Ferrum Mesh
datagram-over-HBONE framing): every datagram is one
`[u16 big-endian length][payload]` record on the stream, in both
directions. Counts cover only what Anvil wrote to and read from the
stream; delivery to the destination is never inferred.

records_sent.description: Records (datagrams) Anvil wrote on the `CONNECT` stream.

records_received.description: Complete records read from the stream.

oversize_refused.description:
Datagrams refused locally, before sending, because they exceed the
65,535 bytes one record can carry.

truncated_tail_bytes.description:
Bytes of an incomplete record the endpoint's stream ended inside
(discarded; never counted as a received datagram).

reset_code.description:
The HTTP/2 error code (name) when the endpoint reset the stream or
the connection (`RST_STREAM` / `GOAWAY`).

oneOf.description: Connection ended without a closing handshake (e.g. WebSocket 1006).

DispatchState.description:
Whether request bytes of an attempt may have reached the peer.

Derived from typed transport state (bytes written to the socket, response
received, HTTP/2 `REFUSED_STREAM`, ...), never from error message text.

oneOf.description:
No request bytes were written (failure before the request was sent), or
the peer explicitly guaranteed non-processing (HTTP/2 REFUSED_STREAM).
The peer received the request (a response to it arrived).
Bytes were written but no response was received; processing may have occurred.

ByteCounts.description:
Byte accounting for one attempt. Logical header sizes on HTTP/2/3 are
estimates (HPACK/QPACK compress headers); `connection_*` counters are
connection-scoped TLS/transport bytes and include other multiplexed streams.

EarlyDataObservation.description:
0-RTT evidence for one attempt. Present only when the early-data opt-in
applied to the attempt.

method_eligible.description: The request method is eligible under the policy.

resumption_attempted.description:
A session ticket was taken from the ticket cache for this connection,
so the ClientHello offered resumption.

resumption_accepted.description:
The server resumed the session (no certificate exchange). `None` when
resumption was not attempted or the handshake did not complete.

offered.description: The ClientHello offered early data and the request was written into it.

accepted.description:
The server accepted (`true`) or rejected (`false`) the early data.
`None` when none was offered or the handshake did not complete.

bytes.description:
Request bytes written before the handshake completed: exact TLS
plaintext over TCP; over HTTP/3 the logical request (estimated QPACK
header size plus body bytes), without QUIC framing.

resent_after_handshake.description:
The server rejected the early data, so the transport sent the same
request again after the handshake. This is how TLS/QUIC deliver
rejected early data (the server discarded it unread), not an
application retry.

tickets_received.description:
Session tickets that arrived for this server and TLS profile while the
attempt ran.

ticket_max_early_data.description:
`max_early_data_size` of the newest ticket that arrived (0: the server
does not allow early data with its tickets).

EarlyDataTransport.description: Which handshake would carry the early data.

oneOf.description: QUIC 0-RTT packets (HTTP/3).
TLS 1.3 early data over TCP (HTTP/1.1 or HTTP/2).

EarlyDataNotUsed.description: Why an attempt covered by the early-data opt-in did not send early data.

oneOf.description:
No session ticket from an earlier connection to this server (same
workspace, TLS profile, client identity, server name and port): a full
handshake, which may deliver tickets for the next request.

A ticket was offered, but the server issued it without permission for
early data (`max_early_data_size = 0`): resumption only.

The method is not eligible (GET, HEAD, OPTIONS, or an idempotent
method the policy lists); the request was sent after the handshake.
An established pooled connection carried the request; no handshake.
The retry after `425 Too Early`: retries are never early data.

The HTTP version policy offers more than one ALPN protocol over TCP,
so the protocol of the early data would be a guess (HTTP/1.1-only or
HTTP/2-only fixes it).

A forward proxy or tunnel carries the connection; early data is only
sent on a direct connection.

The ticket allowed early data, but the handshake completed before the
request was written (a fast path finishes it while HTTP/3 is still
being set up), so the request went out as ordinary data.

wire_bytes.description: Body bytes received from the wire (after transfer decoding, before content decoding).

display_truncated.description:
True when more bytes were received than retained (display cap only —
NOT a wire failure).

decoding.description:
Outcome of content decoding. Absent when the body has no content-coding
or automatic decompression is off.

decoding_detail.description: Why content decoding did not complete.

blob_sha256.description: Content-addressed id of the stored raw (captured) bytes.

oneOf.description: Framing completed normally (content-length satisfied, final chunk, END_STREAM).
The stream ended abnormally before framing completed.
The user or a deadline canceled reading.
Reading stopped at the local `max_response_bytes` ceiling.
No body by protocol (HEAD, 204, 304, 1xx).

ContentDecoding.description:
Outcome of removing the response's content-coding for display,
assertions and extraction. Independent of the body completeness, which
describes the raw bytes on the wire.

oneOf.description: The whole body was decoded.
Decoding stopped at the local `max_decoded_bytes` ceiling; the decoded body is only a prefix.
The content-coding is not supported; the body stays encoded.
The encoded bytes could not be decoded; the body stays encoded.

dropped_messages.description: Messages dropped from the transcript because of the retention bound.

StreamMessage.description: One message/event/datagram in a session transcript (bounded preview).

ExecutionOutcome.description:
The composite outcome. Transport completion, application status and
assertion results are deliberately separate dimensions.

dispatch.description: Summary across all attempts: whether the whole request may have been processed.

TransportState.description: Transport completion, independent of HTTP/RPC status.

oneOf.description: The exchange completed at the transport level (full response framing).
The exchange failed before a response was received.

A response started but did not complete (headers then truncated body,
missing gRPC terminal status, abnormal stream end).

ApplicationState.description:
Application-level result: HTTP status class, gRPC status, SOAP fault,
GraphQL errors. Evaluated only when a response exists.

extensions.description:
Extension negotiation and compression, when an extension was
offered or answered, or a frame claimed one.

masque.description:
Present when the datagrams went through an RFC 9298 CONNECT-UDP
(MASQUE) proxy.

oneOf.description: Status delivered in HTTP trailers.
Status delivered in response headers (trailers-only response).

gRPC-Web: status delivered in the trailer frame (flag `0x80`) at the
end of the response body.
No terminal status was received — the RPC result is unknown.

WsExtensions.description:
WebSocket extension negotiation (RFC 6455 §9) and RFC 7692
`permessage-deflate` evidence for one session.

answered.description:
The server's `Sec-WebSocket-Extensions` answer, verbatim and bounded
(absent: the answer named no extension).

problem.description: Why the answer was refused (`negotiation = rejected`).

traffic.description:
Data messages of the session, before and after compression (absent
when the session never opened).

violation.description:
A received frame broke the compression that was (or was not)
negotiated, and Anvil ended the session.

oneOf.description: Nothing was offered and nothing was answered.
Offered, but the answer named no extension: the session is uncompressed.
`permessage-deflate` is in use.

The answer did not fit the offer, or named an extension that was not
offered; Anvil failed the handshake (RFC 6455 §4.1, RFC 7692 §7).

client_compresses.description:
Anvil compressed the messages it sent. False when the agreed client
window is 2^8 bytes, which Anvil's DEFLATE cannot produce: it then
sends uncompressed messages, which RFC 7692 §6 allows.

WsCompressionTraffic.description: Per-direction data-message totals of a WebSocket session.

messages.description: Text and binary messages whose first frame crossed the wire.

compressed_messages.description: Of those, messages with RSV1 set (compressed).

payload_bytes.description:
Payload bytes of the complete messages, uncompressed (the sizes in
the transcript).

wire_bytes.description:
Data-frame payload bytes on the wire, as sent or received
(compressed where RSV1 was set).

compressed_bytes.description: Compressed bytes of the offending message received when it failed.

limit_bytes.description: Anvil's local message limit, in decompressed bytes.

detail.description: The decompressor's description of the problem.

WsViolationKind.description: Why a received frame ended a session (all are the peer's frames).

oneOf.description:
A data message arrived with RSV1 set although no compression was
negotiated (RFC 6455 §5.2).
A compressed message could not be decompressed (RFC 7692 §7.2.2).

A compressed message grew past Anvil's local message limit while it
was decompressed.

MasqueTunnel.description:
Evidence about an RFC 9298 CONNECT-UDP tunnel through an HTTP/3 proxy.
Counts cover only what Anvil sent and received; delivery to the target
is never inferred.

extended_connect.description:
Whether the proxy's HTTP/3 SETTINGS enabled extended CONNECT
(`None`: no SETTINGS were received).

h3_datagrams.description:
Whether HTTP/3 datagrams were available: the proxy's SETTINGS enabled
`SETTINGS_H3_DATAGRAM` and QUIC negotiated DATAGRAM frames.

connect_status.description: The proxy's HTTP status for the CONNECT-UDP request (`None`: no answer).

encoding.description: The encoding chosen for sending (`None`: the tunnel never opened).

dropped.description:
HTTP Datagrams with an unregistered context ID and capsules of
unknown type, dropped as RFC 9298 §4 / RFC 9297 §3.1 require.

closed_by.description: How the CONNECT stream (the tunnel) ended.

MasqueEncoding.description: How HTTP Datagrams travelled through a CONNECT-UDP tunnel.

oneOf.description: QUIC DATAGRAM frames (quarter stream ID + context ID 0).
RFC 9297 DATAGRAM capsules on the CONNECT stream.

DiagnosticFinding.description: A single diagnostic claim with its evidence and confidence.

alternatives.description: Other explanations consistent with the same evidence.

does_not_prove.description: Statements this evidence does NOT establish (shown explicitly).

confirm_with.description: What additional evidence would confirm or refute the claim.

SourceScope.description: Which leg / owner of the path a claim is about.

oneOf.description: Anvil itself, before any network activity.
Anvil ↔ the peer it connected to (gateway or ordinary destination).
The gateway's own admission/configuration/policy decisions.
The gateway ↔ its upstream backend.
Delivery of an already-started response.

Confidence.description:
Qualitative confidence. Anvil never invents probability percentages.
`Unknown` is a correct answer when evidence is insufficient.

EvidenceSource.description:
Where a piece of evidence came from. Rules weight native measurements and
trusted gateway fields above generic status meanings and body heuristics.

oneOf.description: Parsed body structure (SOAP fault, GraphQL errors). Weak evidence of origin.
Ferrum marker from a destination the user explicitly trusts as Ferrum.
Ferrum-like marker from an unverified destination.
Authenticated gateway diagnostic detail (versioned contract).
The person using Anvil (request, credentials, local settings).
